title: Dakshineswar Kali Temple
visualBrief: Dakshineswar Kali Temple medium-fi compound: the specific cream/red nine-spired Navaratna main shrine with four lower/four upper/one central ridged spires, strongly bowed cornices, five-bay recessed arches, raised platform and south approach; a separate southern Natmandir hall and northern shrine, twelve small red double-curved-roof Shiva shrines along the riverfront split around the central passage, and mapped low courtyard boundary wings. Keep the court open and the Hooghly outside the asset; no large solid compound extrusion.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Q1157765 and way291865633 identify the mapped compound. Standard PMTiles record35184663954465 supplies its precise irregular outer outline; it currently has no courtyard holes or individual temple plans. Replace that one broad native shell with an open compound. Align local east/south about6degrees to the mapped walls. Main-shrine, Natmandir, northern shrine and twelve riverfront-shrine centers/dimensions are explicit picture-led subdivisions inside the boundary, not surveyed footprints. The south-facing main approach and western riverfront give signed orientation. Preserve every independent surrounding map record.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: Daylight pictures guide the main three diminishing bowed stages, four-plus-four-plus-one spire silhouette, cream plaster/red pilasters, ribbed conical-curved crowns, five-bay arcades, plinth and shallow stairs. Main total height is estimated about31m above its approach, with subordinate hall about7m and small riverfront shrines about7m. Fine mouldings, rib counts, sculpture, inscriptions, exact balcony/door patterns and hidden interiors remain simplified; later restoration paint is not independently certified.
